Random start: a Fisher-Yates allocation with exactly n_T = round(n·prob_T) treated (any prob_T in (0,1); errors if that leaves no treated or no control subject). details: Inside the KK GLMM get_likelihood_test_spec(): observed_information, fisher_information and information all return block_diag_information(fit). It takes the analytic expected Fisher information of the Gaussian random-intercept LMM at the null-restricted fit (get_gaussian_lmm_fisher_cpp(X, y, group_id, b)) and sets the beta x (log_sigma_e, log_sigma_b) cross blocks to zero, because the expected information is exactly block-diagonal between the fixed effects and the variance components. This avoids the non-zero cross terms of the observed Hessian at a null-restricted fit, which made it indefinite and sent about 68% of score tests to the ridge fallback (v1.0.6 TODO-167). algorithm: two-start constrained refit (warm start vs full-fit start)
details: In the KK GLMM get_likelihood_test_spec(), fit_null(delta, start) runs fast_gaussian_lmm_cpp with beta_T fixed at delta (L-BFGS, maxit 300, eps_g 1e-6) from the supplied warm start. When a warm start was passed (CI inversion, not the first call), it also refits from the full-fit parameters with beta_T = delta, using run_fit(). It keeps the second fit only if its neg-loglik is lower by more than 1e-4 (nll() helper, Inf for a failed fit). A warm start from another null fit can sit near the sigma_b = 0 boundary, where the log-scale gradient vanishes and L-BFGS reports convergence at a non-optimum. The 1e-4 margin stops optimizer noise (about 1e-5) from making p(delta) jitter and stalling the Newton steps of lrt_ci_nr_cpp (tol_p = 1e-7).
complexity: up to 2 x O(iters n p^2) per null fit

details: Symmetrizes the observed information, eigendecomposes the gamma (loading) block and flags eigenvalues <= tol*max(abs(diag)) (tol = 1e-6) as flat directions, i.e. loadings merged with a neighbouring category or running to +/-Inf. It builds T = blockdiag(I on alpha/beta, retained gamma eigenvectors) and returns T' I T together with the number of flat directions. Consumers (.stereotype_boundary_ssq_b_1, .stereotype_attach_information, stereotype_fit_is_usable) run Cholesky/rcond checks and invert on this reduced matrix, so a boundary MLE is not treated as a failed fit.
complexity: O(p_gamma^3 + P^2 p) for P total parameters

If there are no flat directions it returns the C++ ssq_b_1 unchanged. If there are, it computes chol() and rcond() of the reduced matrix and returns NA unless chol succeeds and rcond > sqrt(.Machine$double.eps). Otherwise it returns chol2inv(ch)[n_alpha + 1, n_alpha + 1], the variance of beta_T.

problem: Reproducible normal deviates for data-seeded multistart perturbations without touching the global RNG
details: Takes a state seed (modulus 2147483647, minimum 1) and iterates the Lehmer/Park–Miller recurrence state = 48271*state mod (2^31-1) to produce 2*ceil(n/2) uniforms, floored at machine epsilon. It pairs them and applies Box–Muller (sqrt(-2 log u1) cos/sin(2 pi u2)), returning the first n deviates. It is deterministic given the seed and never reads or changes .Random.seed. Used to perturb alpha/beta/gamma for the two data-seeded multistart starts.

The caller's warm-start chain and the object's warm Fisher are ignored, so p(delta) depends only on (data, delta). The continuation-ratio fit_null in the same file is still a two-start refit (warm start + full-fit-with-delta nudged +1e-3, keep lower NLL). problem: Draw r allocations with objective ≤ cutoff
details: i.i.d. rejection sampling; each draw is a full Fisher–Yates plus `d = M(2w−1)` (M = L⁻¹X'/n via LLT, or diag-sd). One master seed is taken from R's RNG, and draw s uses its own stream seeded from (master, s), so a candidate depends only on its draw index. Parallel mode runs waves of at most nthreads blocks of 64 draws (OpenMP static). The accepted allocations are merged in block order until r are found, so the accepted set and its order do not depend on thread count or scheduling. Early stopping can overshoot by up to nthreads*64 candidates.
